source: NCERT Class VI, Curiosity: Textbook of Science, Ch. 8.

sections.heading: 1. The Three States of Water
points: Water exists in **three states**: **solid (ice)**, **liquid (water)** and **gas (water vapour / steam)**.
The state depends on **temperature**.
Water is the only common substance found naturally in all three states on Earth.

sections.heading: 2. Changes of State
points: **Melting** — solid → liquid (ice → water) on **heating**; ice melts at **0°C** (melting point).
**Freezing** — liquid → solid (water → ice) on **cooling**; water freezes at **0°C**.
**Evaporation** — liquid → vapour, slowly, at **any temperature** (from the surface).
**Boiling** — liquid → vapour rapidly at a fixed temperature; water **boils at 100°C** (boiling point).
**Condensation** — vapour → liquid on **cooling** (e.g. water droplets on a cold glass).
**Freezing point of water = 0°C; boiling point = 100°C** (at sea level).

sections.heading: 3. Evaporation vs Boiling
points: **Evaporation:** slow, only at the **surface**, at any temperature; causes **cooling** (e.g. sweating cools us, water in earthen pots stays cool).
**Boiling:** fast, throughout the liquid, only at the boiling point.
Evaporation increases with **higher temperature, more surface area, wind, and lower humidity**.

sections.heading: 4. The Water Cycle
points: The continuous movement of water between land, water bodies and the sky:

sub: **Evaporation** — Sun heats water in oceans/rivers → water vapour rises (plants add vapour by **transpiration**).
**Condensation** — vapour cools high up → tiny droplets → **clouds**.
**Precipitation** — droplets grow and fall as **rain, snow or hail**.
**Collection** — water flows back to rivers, lakes and oceans, and the cycle repeats.

points: The water cycle keeps the **supply of fresh water** going; water must be **conserved**.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Three states: solid (ice), liquid (water), gas (vapour); state depends on temperature.
Melting/freezing point of water = 0°C; boiling point = 100°C (at sea level).
Evaporation = slow, surface, any temperature, causes cooling; boiling = fast, at 100°C.
Condensation = vapour → liquid on cooling.
Water cycle: evaporation → condensation → precipitation → collection.
Plants release water vapour by transpiration.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Evaporation happens at any temperature** (only at the surface); **boiling** only at 100°C.
Evaporation causes **cooling** (that's why sweating and earthen pots cool).
Melting/freezing point of water = **0°C**; boiling point = **100°C**.
Droplets on a cold glass form by **condensation** of water vapour in the air (not by leaking).
